focus: sandbox escape, deny bypass, permissions.deny on ctx tools, proxy handling, ADR-0014 redaction, release-branch supply chain

findings.title: v2's proxy-env + SSRF design re-opens a fixed SSRF/DNS-rebinding bug (CWE-918, CWE-441)
findings.claim: TECH-SPEC.md:439 and DECISIONS-r3.md Q19 say only 'Fetch: honours HTTP(S)_PROXY/NO_PROXY, with an SSRF check on the target host' with no mention of stripping proxy env vars inside the fetch subprocess, patching dns.promises/resolve4/resolve6, or a second connect-time re-check.
findings.evidence: git archaeology in cm-main: ef9eeaa4 'close DNS rebinding gap in ctx_fetch_and_index SSRF guard (#476)' shows the parent-process ssrfGuard resolves DNS once, but the real fetch runs in a subprocess that does its own dns.lookup — a low-TTL DNS record can pass the parent check then resolve to 169.254.169.254 (cloud IMDS) at connect time. Follow-up 42448389 'close DNS guard gaps from CR (dns/promises, resolve*, proxy env)' states explicitly: 'the executor DENIED set has zero proxy entries, so HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / ALL_PROXY ... are inherited by every sandbox subprocess. Undici honors these vars by default, which means a configured proxy routes fetch through an arbitrary target -- DNS resolution happens at the proxy and the in-subprocess DNS guard never sees the rebound IP.' The v1 fix strips proxy env vars inside the generated fetch subprocess specifically (not in the executor's global deny list) and patches dns.lookup, dns.promises.lookup, dns.resolve4, dns.resolve6 together, with a pinned test asserting the embedded classifyIp has no module-scope reference. ADR-0012/TECH-SPEC for v2 do not reference any of this.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: ef9eeaa4 and 42448389 (PR #476, cc @aaronjmars @ousamabenyounes). ORIGINAL_INTENT: close an SSRF/DNS-rebinding gap where the parent-process pre-check passes but the subprocess's own DNS resolution (or an inherited HTTP(S)_PROXY) reaches a blocked IP range (e.g. cloud metadata). REGRESSION_RISK: v2 reintroduces exactly this gap if 'honours HTTP(S)_PROXY' is implemented as plain env inheritance without first stripping proxy vars from the fetch subprocess and re-checking at connect time. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: proxy env must be stripped specifically from the ctx_fetch_and_index subprocess (not the general executor deny list, per the v1 Architect note, so ctx_execute user code keeps proxy support); the SSRF classifier must run at DNS-resolution/connect time in the same process that performs the fetch, covering dns.lookup, dns.promises.lookup, dns.resolve4/6; a golden/unit test should pin that the embedded guard has no module-scope closures.
findings.fix: Add to TECH-SPEC/ADR-0012 (or wherever Q19 lands): the fetch subprocess strips HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY and lowercase/npm_config_* variants before allowing a user-opted-in proxy path to be re-applied under the same classifyIp gate; the SSRF check re-verifies the resolved IP at connect time inside the fetch subprocess (not only as a pre-flight in the caller), covering dns.lookup, dns.promises.lookup, dns.resolve4, dns.resolve6; add a GP-series golden test asserting this, mirroring v1 tests/core/server.test.ts.

findings.title: /release skill runs 'npm ci' and 'npm run build', contradicting the owner's 'no npm for v2' decision and reopening a supply-chain surface the release pipeline otherwise tries to close
findings.claim: .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md step 2 says: 'Run the deterministic tests: npm ci && npm run build && node --test e2e/cases'.
findings.evidence: Owner decision on record: 'no npm for v2' (asserted, project rules). ADR-0013 'Maximum release automation' otherwise goes out of its way to avoid npm-shaped release tooling ('release-please and changesets assume an npm package ... A dependency-free script of about 50 lines is used instead') and the release.yml 'build' job text says 'no package.json'. Yet the one owner-facing release entry point still runs npm ci against whatever lockfile/registry state is present at release time, which is exactly the supply-chain surface (arbitrary postinstall scripts, registry compromise, lockfile drift) the rest of ADR-0013 is designed around.
findings.archaeology: Not a v1 regression (no matching v1 commit found for this specific skill step; checked via git log -S "npm ci" --all in cm-main, which returns only unrelated Windows/CI hits), so this is a new v2 authoring inconsistency rather than a re-broken fix — flagged as a doc-decision contradiction per the review's own rule ('a conflict is a finding against the DOC, never a proposal to undo the decision').
findings.fix: Either change SKILL.md step 2 to the v2 no-npm build/test invocation (whatever the 'no npm for v2' decision actually specifies as the build/test runner), or, if npm ci is intentionally retained only for the release skill's own dev-dependency install (separate from the shipped bundle), say so explicitly in ADR-0013/SKILL.md and note the pinned-lockfile / registry-integrity expectation (e.g. npm ci --ignore-scripts, or a provenance check) so a reader cannot read this as silent scope creep back into npm.

findings.title: ADR-0014 Q18 widens the debug-report leak surface the original ADR was written to close, with no re-stated bound on what 'maximum debug data' may still include
findings.claim: ADR-0014 Q18: 'Issue debug data: only secrets are stripped ... Paths, logs, versions, transcript excerpts and the doctor report are required. This replaces ADR-0014's "no path text" rule.'
findings.evidence: The same ADR's 'Why v1 debug output fails' section lists 'Redaction is done with regex and leaks secrets (#1141, #1144, #1155)' as a named v1 failure mode, and section 3 built a typed structural scanner specifically so that 'Paths, env values, config values, file bodies, error messages and command lines cannot reach the output.' Q18 now requires paths, logs and transcript excerpts (the exact categories section 3 excluded) while keeping only a secrets-token filter, but the doc does not re-specify which scanner catches tokens inside free-form transcript excerpts and logs (the structural per-field scanner in section 3 assumed closed-enum fields, not raw log/transcript text).
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY (the fix being partially reversed): ADR-0014 section 3's typed-scanner design, written against v1 bugs #1141/#1144/#1155 (regex redaction leaked secrets). REGRESSION_RISK: once logs and transcript excerpts (free text) are required fields, the typed field-scanner no longer covers the one place secrets most often leak (inline tokens inside pasted log/transcript text), reintroducing the #1141/#1144/#1155 shape of bug through the back door Q18 opened. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: whatever strips tokens from logs/transcripts must be specified (and golden-tested per GP11) with the same rigor as the structural scanner, not left to 'only secrets are stripped' as a one-line intent.
findings.fix: Add an explicit mechanism (and a GP11-style golden test case) for secret-stripping inside free-form log/transcript text specifically, separate from the structural per-field scanner in ADR-0014 section 3, since Q18 now routes exactly that free text into the report.
